text: Welcome to your bistro! Before shopping, let's plan today's cooking. Open your recipe book: Recipes, in the top bar.
Each card is a dish. Press + on one dish you'd like to cook today. Dishes you can't afford yet are greyed out.
Your plan is set! The panel in the top-left now tracks what this dish still needs. Close the recipe book to go shopping.
Now let's buy what your dish needs. Click a food type in the plan panel to see where to find it, or click a store on the map.
Welcome in! Each aisle is a shelf: click one to see what's on it. The same food can cost different amounts in different stores.

Press + on a food card, or drag it onto your cart, to add a package. Click a card to flip it and read its label. When the plan panel shows nothing missing, check out. After that first purchase, you can shop as often as you like.

Sort each new food into Green, Yellow or Red. Green foods are the everyday foundation and the only foods that build health. Yellow foods are ones customers are moving away from. Red foods are the ones to avoid. Flip a card to read its ingredients. Each new food you sort correctly gives back {maxDiscount} of what you paid for it. Answers are final once you submit.
Back at the market! You can visit other stores and check out again; each purchase gets its own quick sort. When you're done shopping, click your Bistro on the map to start cooking.
Time to cook! Pick a recipe you have ingredients for. Faded recipes are missing something.

Drag one serving at a time from your pantry into the recipe's slots. A red outline means a slot still needs something. Drag a row out of a slot to put it back. For your first dish, fill every slot exactly, then press Review dish.

Your first dish is done! You used {ingredients}. Health changed by {healthDelta}, and it covered these Daily Dozen groups: {dailyDozen}. Only Green foods build health. Each Daily Dozen group a guest hasn't had before adds a little extra, so vary the plants you serve. From now on, you can also serve dishes that don't match the recipe, but guests will notice.

That guest felt a quick burst of energy, then a slump. A rush can feel good in the moment, but it doesn't mean the meal was good for them. Judge a meal by what's in it, not by how lively a guest seems afterwards.

A letter from the landlord: from tomorrow, rent of ${rent} is due every morning. You can only shop while you have money, so keep a little cushion. Busy evenings bring in takeaway income, and guests will soon start arriving with requests.

Money is running low, and tomorrow's rent could leave you unable to shop. Open Pantry, drag food you won't use onto SELL, then press Sell. Food that would spoil before you cook it is the best thing to sell.

From today, guests may ask for something, like Savory, Creamy or Crunchy. Each recipe shows what it answers. Answering a request delights a guest and grows your popularity. Each request a dish leaves unanswered costs {missedCraving} popularity, even when the dish itself is built right. Health still comes only from the foods you choose.

Your pantry couldn't make any recipe, so a local farmer brought a small crate of plain staples, enough for one simple dish. The farmer can only help once a day, so shop or sell spare food to get back on your feet.

You have {totalDays} days to make your bistro's name. Each day: shop, sort what's new, then cook for your guests. Rent starts on day {rentStart}, and guests bring requests from day {cravingsStart}. At the end, your popularity and the community's wellbeing decide how the story ends.

Popularity is how well known your bistro is. More guests come at {guestThresholds} popularity (up to {maxGuests}), and above {walkInThreshold}, walk-in customers buy takeaway every evening. Delighted guests, answered requests and tasty plates raise it; mismatched dishes and ignored requests lower it.

Guests pay you, plus tips, for every dish, and the market takes your money for food. From day {rentStart}, rent of ${rent} is due each morning. You can only shop while you have money, and ending deep in debt closes the bistro. Short on cash? Sell spare food from the Pantry.
This is your pantry: the food you own. Each card shows its servings and how many days are left before it spoils. At the market you can sell pantry food back for {sellRate} of what you paid.
These are today's guests. Some ask for something special. Meeting a request helps your popularity; ignoring it can hurt it.
Hmm, that store isn't open yet. I wonder what's inside... Keep an eye on the News.
Closed today? Darn. Events can close a store for a while. Try another store, and check the News to see when it reopens.
Heads up: an event has closed a store today. Open the News to see what happened.
New recipes are in your book today! Open Recipes to see what's new, and plan them with +.
Back for more? You can shop at as many stores as you like each day. Each purchase gets its own quick sort.
Not every answer was right this time. Foods you got wrong come back on a later purchase, so you'll get another try.
You skipped a guest. That saves your ingredients, but they leave without a meal.
That dish didn't match its recipe exactly. Fill every slot with the right food type to build the full recipe.
Your guests will wait while you shop. Click your Bistro on the map to go back to them.
Some food in your pantry spoils tomorrow. It's a good day to cook with it, or you can sell it while you're at the market. A quick peek at the pantry each morning helps you spot what to use first.

Your dish was built right, but popularity went down a little. That's because it didn't answer what this guest asked for: each missed request costs {missedCraving} popularity. Before picking a recipe, check the guest's request; each recipe card shows which requests it answers.

This guest would like something comforting. Comfort isn't tied to one recipe: any dish whose ingredients have an average appeal of {comfort} or more answers it. You can see each food's appeal in the corner of its card.
